role.altitude: The vending machine servicer keeps diagnosing, repairing, filling machines, counting cash and finding the cause of shortfalls; copying paper forms into spreadsheets, reading counters, looking up part numbers and adding up daily totals shrink.
skills_to_grow: Closing work orders on the phone at the machine
role.ambitious_version: A servicer who arrives knowing what each machine sold and what is broken, carrying the right parts and products.

tasks.short: Look up the machine's history, record the fault, cause, parts and times of machine maintenance and repair, transfer records to the office system and correct incomplete records.

steps.what: Servicer looks up the machine's maintenance and repair history before the job
Servicer records the fault, cause, parts used and times of the machine repair

loop.input: The servicer's voice note about the job.
loop.output: Draft job text and a suggested fault code from the company's list.
loop.check: The servicer confirms the text and picks or changes the code before closing the work order.
loop.stop: If no code fits, the job goes to the service planner to code.
loop.why_not_simpler: Servicers describe faults in their own words, often with gloves on.

steps.what: Servicer types the paper job sheets into the office system
Servicer corrects records flagged as incomplete

tasks.design: Each machine carries a code label. The servicer scans it to open the work order on the phone with the machine's history. At the end of the job they close the work order with fault and cause pick lists, parts and start and stop times; a voice note can be turned into draft text with a suggested fault code, which the servicer confirms. The record then sits in the office system without retyping. Required fields stop most incomplete records. Time stamps are used for the job record, not to rate servicers, and this is agreed with the works council first.
tasks.previous_blocker: Paper job sheets were retyped at the end of the day.
tasks.enabler_now: Mobile work orders with pick lists, label scanning and voice notes.
tasks.still_hard: Machines without labels from other owners.
tasks.human_edge: Writing down the cause that matters for the next repair.

reach.learn: Whether fault codes show which machines fail most.

evidence.claim: A maintenance app transcribes voice memos into the work order.
A fibre network firm reported about 8 hours per technician per week saved on work-order mail, entry and reports after moving to mobile work orders.
Work orders with time stamps or location can observe technicians and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: records of maintenance and repair; the repair itself is outside.
Input contract for s3: records come from work orders closed on the phone in s2; about 90% of machines carry labels; jobs on unlabelled machines are still typed; s3 is priced at that share.
Recording on the phone takes most of the time paper took.
research_questions: Do repeat repairs fall when history is at hand?

already_counted.description: Servicer corrects drafted text and suggested fault codes.

incremental.description: Servicer labels new or relocated machines.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many unlabelled machines and little phone use; high: 90% labelled machines, all jobs closed on the phone.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Decide which parts are needed, find part numbers, prepare the order request for parts needed for machine repairs, have it approved and sent, and track delivery.

steps.what: Servicer decides which parts are needed for the machine repairs
Servicer finds the part numbers in manuals and supplier catalogues

loop.input: The servicer's description of the part and the machine model from the work order.
loop.output: Matching catalogue lines with part number, picture and price.
loop.check: The servicer confirms the match against the picture and the machine model.
loop.stop: If nothing matches, the servicer looks the part up in the manual.
loop.why_not_simpler: Servicers name parts differently from suppliers' catalogues.

steps.what: Servicer prepares the order request
Buyer approves the final order request
Buyer sends the approved order to the supplier
Servicer tracks delivery and follows up late parts

approvals.approved_version: the order request as approved by the buyer in s4; any change goes back for approval

tasks.design: From the work order, the servicer describes the part and a search matches it to supplier catalogue lines for that machine model, with a picture to confirm. The confirmed lines become an order request routed to the buyer, who approves and sends it. Delivery status shows on the work order, and the servicer is notified when parts arrive. Deciding which parts are needed stays with the servicer.
tasks.previous_blocker: Part numbers were looked up in paper manuals and orders sent by mail.
tasks.enabler_now: Supplier catalogues linked to work orders and purchase systems.
tasks.still_hard: Parts for old machines no longer in catalogues.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether to replace a part or the whole unit.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and chasing; deciding stays.

reach.learn: Whether requests arrive with correct part numbers.

evidence.claim: A bounded model step can match free-text parts to catalogue lines, with a buyer approving.

assumptions: Boundary: ordering parts for repairs; paying invoices is outside.
Input contract for s2: catalogues of the main suppliers loaded in the purchase system by the buyer, covering about 70% of parts; s2 is priced at that share.
Deciding keeps its full time; the buyer's time is outside the servicer's savings.
unknowns: Share of parts in loaded catalogues.

incremental.description: Servicer reports wrong catalogue matches to the buyer.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: old machines with few catalogue parts; high: current models at 70% catalogue coverage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read sales counters, count cash, record transaction information, compare cash with sales, find the cause of gaps, notify designated personnel of discrepancies and file the forms.

steps.what: Servicer reads sales counters and writes them on the collection form
Servicer counts the cash and coins collected
Servicer records transaction information: the cash count per machine
Servicer compares collected cash with sales to spot discrepancies
Servicer checks the machine for the cause of a gap: jam, coin mechanism fault or break-in
Servicer notifies designated personnel of discrepancies
Servicer hands in and files the paper collection forms

tasks.design: Telemetry units in the machines send sales counts to the vending management system, so the servicer no longer reads and writes counters; machines without telemetry are read on the phone. The servicer counts cash and enters the total on the phone. A rule compares cash with sales and flags gaps above a set amount. The servicer checks the machine for the cause, and the flag notifies the named person in the finance office with the servicer's note. The phone record replaces paper forms.
tasks.previous_blocker: Counters were read by hand and gaps found when the office added up forms days later.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine telemetry and mobile collection records.
tasks.still_hard: Gaps from coins stuck in the mechanism versus theft.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing signs of a break-in or tampering.

ambition.what: Check cash against sales at every visit instead of weekly in the office.

tasks.altitude: Much less writing and adding up; counting and checking stay.

evidence.claim: A US vending operator using telemetry halved the drivers on its San Francisco routes and raised fills per visit by 75%.
Telemetry can feed sales and cash, and a rule can flag a count gap above a set amount to a named person.
Records with time stamps or location can observe staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: transaction records and discrepancy reports for collections; banking the cash is outside.
Input contract for s1: telemetry units fitted by the operator send sales counts; about 80% of machines have them; the rest are read on the phone; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s7: the record entered on the phone in s3 replaces the paper form.
Cash counting and finding causes keep their full time.

incremental.description: Servicer checks telemetry counts against the machine counter on a sample of visits.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few machines with telemetry; high: 80% telemetry coverage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Note merchandise filled per machine, record money collected, update van stock, keep records of merchandise distributed and money collected in the daily report, and check and sign the totals.

steps.what: Servicer notes merchandise filled per column
Servicer records the cash count per machine
Servicer updates the van stock list
Servicer totals the day's merchandise and money in the daily report
Servicer checks the daily totals and signs them

tasks.design: Telemetry sends sales per column since the last visit, so the fill per column is known before the servicer opens the machine; the servicer confirms or corrects the fill on the phone. Cash is entered as a count per machine. Confirmed fills lower the van stock list, and the daily report totals merchandise and money from these records instead of a spreadsheet. The servicer checks and signs the totals.
tasks.previous_blocker: Fills and cash were written on route sheets and added up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Machine telemetry and mobile route records.
tasks.still_hard: Products swapped between columns without updating the planogram.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing that a total does not fit the day.
tasks.altitude: Much less writing and adding; checking stays.

reach.learn: Whether van loads match what machines need.

evidence.claim: A US vending operator using telemetry raised fills per visit by 75% and halved drivers on its San Francisco routes.
Records with time stamps or location can observe staff and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: records of merchandise and money per route; filling the machines is outside.
Input contract for s1: telemetry units fitted by the operator report sales per column; about 80% of machines have them; the rest are counted and entered on the phone; s1 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s3 and s4: fills confirmed in s1 and cash entered in s2.
Checking and signing keep their full time.

incremental.description: Servicer updates the column layout when products change.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few machines with telemetry; high: 80% telemetry coverage.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
